publisher: UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and Home Office
title: Cyber Security Breaches Survey 2025/2026
population: UK businesses with at least one employee and an online presence; public-sector organisations and sole traders are excluded
design: random-probability survey, predominantly telephone, weighted by business size, sector and region
marginOfError: ±1.6 to ±2.6 percentage points for overall business estimates at 95% confidence, based on effective sample sizes

prevalence.definition: Any cyber security breach or attack identified in the previous 12 months. This is not equivalent to a material financial loss event.

materialFinancialCost.definition: Among organisations identifying a breach or attack, the share whose most disruptive breach had a non-zero perceived financial cost.
materialFinancialCost.derivation: Non-zero-cost base divided by all-business base in Tables 4.2a and 4.1a. The bases are rounded published survey bases, not an exact respondent cross-tabulation.

negativeOutcome.definition: Businesses reporting any negative outcome from a breach or attack in the previous 12 months; not used directly as the materiality likelihood because it is measured across the whole business sample.

positiveCostSeverity.definition: Perceived total cost of the most disruptive breach or attack among respondents reporting a non-zero cost. One incident per responding organisation; not an annual sum of all incidents.

scenarioComposition.note: The survey reports breach types, but those categories do not map one-to-one to the five scenarios and do not provide an organisation-level annual scenario frequency. Scenario weights remain a weak elicitation prior and must be sensitivity-tested.

limitations: Only identified and reported breaches are observed; hidden, unreported and unmonitored events are omitted.
Costs are perceived and mainly cover the most disruptive incident, not all annual losses.
The non-zero-cost ratio is derived from rounded published bases rather than an exact cross-tabulation.
The survey is UK-specific and excludes sole traders and most public-sector organisations.
Detection and reporting practices vary by organisation size; lower small-organisation prevalence may partly reflect weaker detection.
Table bases include unweighted counts; model effective sample size must account for survey weighting and transportability.
permittedUses: validation of reference-class predictions against later consistent survey waves
prohibitedUses: treating any breach or attack as a material loss event
treating the most disruptive incident cost as annual total loss
mapping breach-type percentages directly to the five scenario annual rates
claiming organisation-specific validation from a national survey
